weeklyStandup.body:
# Marin standup — Week ending Fri, Nov 13, 2026

**Previous standup**: [Week of November 2, 2026 standup](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11169)

## Amy Sartran ([@asartran](https://github.com/asartran))

### What you did this week

- Got the Snowball training loop ready, 2 nodes of MI355x. Checkpointing, restarts and real data all work. Built the Snowball-mix ladder datasets on GCS, and drafted an outline for a decontaminated Harrier training set for the full snowball run.
- Mostly reviewing and benchmarking Marco’s AMD PR stack(#11122-#11126, #11140-#11148, #11150-#11159). We’re reworking to avoid touching too much of the model config and having AMD-specific implementation logic outside the training code.
- Some CI fixes. One makes pre-commit catch stale vendored lockfiles, which failed 87 CI jobs last week ([#11423](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11423)). The other fixes one of the two failures that have broken the nightly slow job since Nov 3 [#11425](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11425), [#11427](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11427).

### What you plan to do next week

- Finish writing the Snowball run plan and send AMD the dataset and storage sizes.
- Review Marco’s restructured PRs and Pratik’s checkpointing fix (supercedes our [#10969](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10969)).
- Build the Harrier ladder caches once the decontamination question is settled.

## Ben Feuer ([@penfever](https://github.com/penfever))

### What you did this week

- Debugged the long loop, landed the first snowball transfer recipe
- Lots of refinements to the RL Data Atlas; data cleaning, ingestion, improved metadata documenting things like what backends support what RL datasets, etc
- Meetings

### What you plan to do next week

- Land more vetted Snowball recipes
- Continue to clean RL + SFT data and ingest new sources

### Blockers / worries / questions

- Getting everyone on the same loop and working from the same RL Data Atlas

## Betsy Cannon ([@forklady42](https://github.com/forklady42))

### What you did this week

- reviewed design and code of TaskForge, including the high level design of the refactor
- dove into TaskForge generated tasks; filed bugs and reviewed quality of tasks

### What you plan to do next week

- code review of TaskForge refactor
- continued quality check of generated tasks

## Chris McConnell ([@chrismc91](https://github.com/chrismc91))

### What you did this week

- Began implementing new evals as potential policy additions [[see evals tracker](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1HSKo2TA9efeEBpTnmWr7PRfebk42WTbSK5vJ6rrauF8/edit?gid=0#gid=0)]
- Design doc on updating how our eval policy is organized in our code [[doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1PSSQ99-miw1kOoxBWamAWNk2t4Aji8UNC4oUau4f35k/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.9hr5c795xfhh)]
- [Early model scorecard](https://applets.marina.oa.dev/a/58367197-a444-4cbd-b080-5ffd8d0b8034/v/2/), started running evals for candidate baseline models

### What you plan to do next week

- Continue with ID benchmark implementations, try to finalize ID benchmark selection
- Finalize baselines for Mochi
- Continue foundations work (policy code organization, scorecard)
- Design docs [Eval lite with Will, eval “list” to give viz on eval implementation status to community with Zack]

### Blockers / worries / questions

- Are other people working on failure mode discovery loops? It’s on my mind, just want to make sure someone is covering this (can be me).

## David Hall ([@dlwh](https://github.com/dlwh))


### What you plan to do next week

- Catch up on the loop

### Blockers / worries / questions

- I am… out of the loop 🕶️

## David Lundgren ([@davidlundgren](https://github.com/davidlundgren))

## Matt Wittmann ([@mcwitt](https://github.com/mcwitt))

### What you did this week

- concluded 262k context extension experiments, choosing the log-scaled version [#11044](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11044)

- moved 17 superseded hero checkpoints (~73 TB) to the empty 01a bucket and deleted them from 02a
- swarmed with Romain and Ahmad on mochi vLLM + MarinSkyRL fixes
- [vLLM inference speed hill-climbing](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11430): full CUDA graphs, tuned GB200 MoE GEMM config, NCCL symmetric memory; ~56 → 19 ms/token
- Lean RL data: reviewed and merged Robert George’s Lean v4.34.1 proof grader + ProofNet-Verified ([#10879](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10879)) and NuminaMath-LEAN training data ([#11095](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11095))

### What you plan to do next week

- draft ragged a2a blog post (/MoK w/ Mark?)
- loop optimization work
- push Lean grader image; smoke-test

Built client-management API, used it to set up Disky’s prod and dev login clients. Scaffolded auth against Google Groups membership, fixed 1-click sign-in across deploys.

### What you plan to do next week

## Tim O'Donnell ([@timodonnell](https://github.com/timodonnell))

### What you did this week

- Worked with Chris and MfS team to sort out process for external people submitting evals and data. For now, they should make their own repo, tell us about it on discord, and we will take a look and track progress on it on Chris’s new evals spreadsheet, and eventually submit it to marin if we decide to include it. Similar for RL data but no spreadsheet yet

- MfS - finalize first round of evals and plan out data generation at a bigger scale
- Clean up pdbthink benchmark and RL data and write a short report on what we did (probably will be a blog post eventually)

sourceStates.title: [skyrl] Adopt the vLLM wheel with batch-invariant NCCL algorithms
sourceStates.body:
SkyRL installs a vLLM wheel whose batch-invariant mode keeps NCCL's Ring and Tree algorithms enabled, so vLLM engine processes can run AllGather under NCCL 2.32.6. The wheel is [marin-vllm-gpu-20261124-7e9b413a5daf](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/releases/tag/marin-vllm-gpu-20261124-7e9b413a5daf); its initializer sets `NCCL_ALGO=ring,tree;allreduce:tree` (marin-community/vllm#139), the value SkyRL's learner and Ray workers use, so the learner takes the value from the initializer. The previous wheel's initializer set `NCCL_ALGO=allreduce:tree`, which leaves AllGather without an algorithm under NCCL 2.32.6, and the GPU nightly's disaggregated rollout test failed with `NCCL error: invalid usage`.

The wheel also carries the fork's GrugMoE and speculative-decoding changes since the previous pin: full decode graphs and GB200 expert GEMM tuning, Triton MoE workspace reservation, padding-logit clearing before expert selection, ShortConv output writes, dense speculative drafts kept out of expert-parallel groups, and DSpark serving for Grug drafts. The release passed the fork's H100 and GB200 wheel qualification. In `vendor/skyrl/uv.lock` only the `vllm` entries change, and `uv lock --check` passes.

The [SkyRL GPU nightly on this branch](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/45365513133) passed all three H100 lanes, including the Grug Megatron suite and its disaggregated rollout test. Snowball `eval-short` on eight H100s scored all 1,500 EvalLite tasks with a mean of 0.588; the previous wheel scored 0.555 on the same model and tasks before grader changes on main, so the two are not directly comparable. sourceStates.title: [rl] Restore checkpoints with CPU-offloaded Adam metadata
sourceStates.body:
Restoring a Megatron checkpoint saved with a CPU-offloaded optimizer fails under torch's restricted weights_only loading: HybridDeviceOptimizer pickles its CPU and GPU optimizer classes into common.pt, and the loader rejects them as untrusted globals.

Stage the checkpoint's metadata files inside a safe_globals scope that allows exactly the runtime's optimizer classes (AdamW and Megatron's Adam). Unrelated checkpoint globals still fail closed, so model-only exports keep restricted Torch loading.

sourceStates.title: [rl] Bound PPO vocabulary memory before rollout admission
sourceStates.body:
Long packed trajectories can exhaust trainer memory after rollouts finish: PPO materializes a full token-by-vocabulary output projection and its backward. Add two opt-in Megatron policy options, both absent from resolved recipes until a recipe sets them, so existing launch identities stay unchanged.

`output_projection_chunk_size` computes token log-probs and entropy through a token-chunked projection with a recomputed backward and native gradient accumulation, instead of a full vocabulary tensor (TP1 PPO without sequence parallelism). `memory_profile` runs a warm-Adam capacity check on every policy rank before initial weight publication and rollout admission: it initializes the optimizer, measures forward, backward and optimizer steps at each configured token count plus `trainer.algorithm.max_seq_len`, and requires a configured device-memory headroom fraction. Sizing restores model, master shards, optimizer, scheduler and random state afterwards, and an enabled check requires explicit capacity and headroom.

sourceStates.title: [eval] Retire Harbor from SkyRL and curated corpus acquisition
sourceStates.body:
Run SkyRL's SWESmith training and three fixed checkpoint cohorts from executable TaskSpecs. RolloutEngine owns Pi and Terminus-2 execution, sandbox setup, and verifier grading. SkyRL's model client supplies the sampled token IDs, log probabilities, and policy metadata used by the learner. The rollout pool retains the 256-machine training limit and records setup exit codes for task-health filtering. Checkpoint selection pools verifier scores by scored-task count and applies its existing coverage thresholds. ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph before["Before · Harbor-backed tasks"] direction LR packages["Harbor task packages"] --> adapter["SkyRL rollout worker
RolloutEngine's Harbor adapter"] adapter --> harbor["Harbor trial
Sandbox, agent, verifier"] harbor <-->|Model turns| oldModel["SkyRL model serving"] harbor --> oldOutput["SkyRL
Training batch or checkpoint scores"] end subgraph after["After · Shared TaskSpec path"] direction LR specs["Curated TaskSpecs"] --> worker["SkyRL rollout worker"] worker --> engine["RolloutEngine
Sandbox, agent, verifier"] engine <-->|Model turns| model["SkyRL model client
Sampled token IDs and log probabilities"] engine --> output["SkyRL
Training batch or checkpoint scores"] end before ~~~ after ``` SkyRL routes live single-turn tasks, agent episodes, and checkpoint evaluation through RolloutEngine. Static preference-pair training reads completions from the dataset. Launching the frozen Micro210 evaluation on this runtime requires the separate migration in #12249. A timed-out agent can still earn a workspace verdict with zero sampled tokens. SkyRL keeps that verdict and masks the empty response from training loss. With an explicit setup timeout, Pi starts its agent time limit after setup, including the time before its first model request. A fresh Daytona verifier with a declared script judge uses a machine-local relay with the grader’s request timeout. The provider credential stays on the host. Setup timeouts and signal exits qualify for infrastructure retry, and ordinary setup exits contribute to task-health filtering. Acquire Terminal-Bench 2.1 directly from the pinned public Harbor Hub release. New downloads are checked against their package digests. The release retains its 89 tasks, cache identity, and layout. SkyRL's entrypoints and wheel no longer require the Harbor runtime. The standalone evaluator and open trial policy still use it. The published SWESmith selection converts all 5,608 SWESmith records and preserves the 105,608 training rows, held-out data, source quotas, and group mix. All 90 checkpoint TaskSpecs were checked against their pinned package contents. The two-H100 SkyRL run at `ae14f60cbe` graded all four Pi trajectories. It carried 994 sampled tokens with aligned log probabilities into one unskipped optimizer step and published the step-1 checkpoint. [SWESmith selection](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-02a%2Fmarin%2Frl-data%2Ftask-selection%2Fsnowball-100k-agentic-pi%2F2026.11.19.2) · [Checkpoint cohort audit](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fpower%2Fcheckpoint-cohorts-verified-20261124-806b87f) · [Optimizer run](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fpower%2Fskyrl-swesmith-final-20261125-ae14f60c%2Fpower-skyrl-swesmith-migration-smoke-2026.11.25.1-a0ffb0d6f520) The checkpoint smoke at `806b87f577` used Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct on one H100, one trial at a time, and one pinned task per cohort. sourceStates.title: [verifyit] Restore grading for unit chains and ordinals
sourceStates.body:
References with compound unit chains, ordinal superscripts, or signed and spaced unit powers now grade against their numeric value. Since #11989, the reference parser rejected a `/\mathrm{s}` tail, read `11^{\text{th}}` as a symbolic exponent, and rejected `\text{s}^{-1}`.

The parser recognizes complete terminal unit chains, accepts bare powers after text groups with nonletter content, and removes ordinal suffixes only from numbers at the start of a reference. This preserves grading for unit strings such as `\text{m/s}^2` and option references such as `\textbf{(C)}\ 11^{\text{th}}`. Text groups followed by additional math retain the existing fail-closed path.

The focused math-answer suite passed 205 tests. The affected runner passed 1,954 Harbor unit tests, 21 Harbor runtime tests, 67 Harbor driver tests, and 933 Marin and VerifyIt tests before the 600-second session limit stopped that lane with no reported failure.

sourceStates.title: [eval] Grade chat tasks on the final answer and require a selection
sourceStates.body:
Every chat evaluation item now states its response selection. `ChatGeneration`, `chat_item`, `chat_variant_item` and `chat_source` no longer default to `combine`, which graded `reasoning + "\n\n" + content`. The tasks that relied on that default now grade the final answer (`final_only`). These are GPQA, mmlu-redux, MRCR, GraphWalks, IFBench, NUPA, JEEBench, SimpleQA, OlympiadBench, AMC23 and FinanceBench, plus the chat variants of HumanEval+, MBPP+, CRUXEval and every compiled lm-eval chat variant. MATH500, AIME and MMLU-Pro keep their content-first selections.

Under `combine`, a model that returns reasoning separately failed MRCR, whose answer must start with the nonce, and could fail IFBench's strict checks. OlympiadBench took the first `\boxed` anywhere in that text. Its prompt ends with "Mark your solution with \boxed", and models often quote that line or write a `\boxed{}` placeholder while reasoning. Either became an empty answer that scored 0 without reaching the judge, which zeroed 56 to 215 of each panel model's 300 trials. OlympiadBench now takes the final answer's last box, as AIME does, and AMC23 drops inline reasoning before its last box. Final-answer grading also scores a reply cut off mid-reasoning as empty. Under `combine`, a letter or box inside such a trace could still earn credit.

Regrading the saved responses of 2026-11-23 runs from main gave the table below, with no new generations. OlympiadBench is the full 30 × 10 at 64K tokens with the gpt-oss-120b judge. Its 717 newly unresolved last-box answers were sent to the same judge with each item's archived request. The other rows come from 20-item smoke runs. Cells show main → this branch.

| Benchmark | Nemotron 3.5 Super | Snowball v0.1 | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B | Glimmer 30B | Mochi SFT |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| OlympiadBench | 32.0 → 69.2 | 35.0 → 55.3 | 37.7 → 74.3 | 19.3 → 45.7 | 28.8 → 60.2 |
| MRCR | 30 → 30 | 16 → 16 | 91 → 91 | 0 → 67 | 25 → 25 |
| IFBench | 30 → 30 | 25 → 25 | 30 → 30 | 25 → 65 | 25 → 25 |
| GPQA Diamond | 87 → 80 | 58 → 58 | 85 → 85 | 78 → 78 | 85 → 85 |

Nemotron's GPQA drop comes from 8 of 60 attempts that hit the token cap mid-reasoning. Glimmer's template cannot disable reasoning, so it carries the MRCR and IFBench changes. The Mochi checkpoint was served without a reasoning parser, so only the OlympiadBench scorer change affects it. On this sample, GSM8K, NUPA, TriviaQA, MATH500, AIME24 and MMLU-Pro do not move. The changed HumanEval+, MBPP+ and CRUXEval answers of Glimmer and Snowball were not re-executed.

Protocols whose item builder selects internally get version 2026.11.24, so their corpora are rebuilt rather than reused. The others change identity through their builder arguments or scorer revision.

sourceStates.title: [levanter] Shadow the most-loaded experts outside ragged EP transport
sourceStates.body:
The ragged all-to-all clips each receiver's capacity block, so assignments above the capacity factor are dropped. Hero SFT data concentrates load on a few experts: late in the production run, 0.88% of assignments were dropped, and 15% in layer 47.

- `ShadowExperts(count, rows_per_token)` makes every shard of an expert-parallel group compute the group's `count` most-loaded experts for its own tokens, with their weights broadcast by a masked psum over `expert`. The choice uses the counts the transport already gathers, on every step and layer. Those assignments skip the all-to-all, and the receivers' capacity goes to the other experts. Each shard computes at most `ceil(rows_per_token * tokens)` rows; the rest goes through the transport.
- The broadcast's backward sums the weight gradients in float32. In bf16 it rounded at every step of the reduction.
- `moe_mlp`, `MoEExpertMlp` and the Hero `GrugModelConfig` take `shadow_experts`, which requires ragged_all_to_all on an expert axis. The dropless callers clear it, and Hero export identity omits it. The new field changes the Hero SFT recipe fingerprint, so the pin in `test_recipe_identities.py` is updated; that step has no expected-fingerprint gate.

One GB200 rack, restored from the SFT checkpoint `step-399500`, 150 paired updates on the same batches:

| | CF 1.625 | `ShadowExperts(6, 1.5)`, CF 1.5 |
|---|---|---|
| drops, mean | 0.88% | 0.053% |
| drops, worst layer | 15.1% (L47) | 0.95% (L7) |
| step time | 23.35 s | 24.35 s (+4.3%) |
| peak memory | 131.4 GiB | 130.8 GiB |

Limitations:
- Step time was measured before the float32 gradient sum, which doubles the bytes of one backward all-reduce.
- Dropless held-out SFT loss drifted +1e-4 over 150 updates, and the router moved load off the top experts of the hottest layers. A 500-update run is in progress.
- On kept assignments the function matches up to rounding.

The new tests compare the clip mask, exact drop counts, and values and gradients, including padding, against a numpy model and a dense reference; they pass on GB200 (bf16, QuACK). A CPU emulation of the ragged all-to-all, not checked in, passed 23 edge cases.

sourceStates.title: [mochi] Enable DSpark for one-rack RL
sourceStates.body:
Enable four-proposal DSpark for one-rack Mochi RL from the pinned step-400407 initializer. The default uses the interleaved 766M two-layer draft at a 0.775 vLLM memory fraction. Standard and agentic one-rack presets inherit the setting. Three-rack presets use plain decoding pending measurements at 262k context with FlashInfer.

Keep Speculators for draft fitting and Levanter for assistant masks. Seeded sampling interleaves the SFT sources by sampled row count and keeps the first-user prompt holdout. Both draft sizes share a prepared dataset and teacher activations. Prefill once on the teacher gang, then fit each draft as a checkpoint ArtifactStep on one GPU. The cache is reusable for 48 hours from prefill start.

### Five-update one-rack comparison

All three runs used Mochi step 400407, the same workload, and 60 GB200s. Plain used a 0.75 memory fraction. Both drafts used four proposals and 0.775.

| Metric | Plain | Prior 521M | Interleaved 766M |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Startup before update 1 | 12m03s | 16m24s | 14m02s |
| Update 1 | 40m40s | 30m52s | 28m48s |
| Mean update, updates 2–3 | 4m38s | 2m22s | 2m16s |
| Update 5 | 14m59s | 16m24s | 9m46s |
| Total updates 2–5 | 34m18s | 27m21s | 21m32s |
| Median update, updates 2–5 | 7m47s | 4m18s | 4m47s |
| Successful rollout call p95, updates 2–5 | 23m17s | 15m23s | 15m20s |
| Lead GPU task wall time | 89m23s | 76m03s | 65m52s |

The 766M cut total warm update time by 37% versus plain and 21% versus the prior draft. The two drafts had similar times in updates 2–3. On update 5, rollout admission took 449 s with the 766M and 840 s with the prior draft. Startup runs from lead GPU task start to the first rollout-wait window. Task wall time excludes the scheduling queue. The p95 pools successful rollout calls dispatched during updates 2–5. [Five-update analysis](https://loom.oa.dev/s/heul67oq/artifacts/mochi-dspark-performance) · [Per-step timings](https://loom.oa.dev/s/heul67oq/artifacts/mochi-dspark-step-time)

Warm trainer–vLLM mean absolute log ratios on fresh tokens were 0.00951, 0.00967, and 0.01033 for plain, 521M, and 766M. The arms had 488k, 358k, and 243k fresh tokens respectively, so coverage differed. The 766M reached 3.077 acceptance length on the shared holdout versus 2.759 for the prior draft, with 119.4k KV tokens per GPU versus 132.2k. The interleaved 521M was preempted twice before completing an RL update. [Ablation records](https://loom.oa.dev/s/heul67oq/artifacts/mochi-dspark-ablation)

### Use the draft on another branch

Use the permanent CoreWeave export with the step-400407 verifier and the Nov 24 ShortConv vLLM wheel. Add these options to a one-rack Mochi launch. [Draft files](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-08a%2Fmarin%2Fcheckpoints%2Fdspark%2Fmochi%2Fablation-interleaved-two-layer%2F2026.11.25-skyrl) · [Verifier export](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8089#issuecomment-6841382920) · [vLLM wheel](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/releases/tag/marin-vllm-gpu-20261124-36cef9c0caf3)

sourceStates.title: [rl] Make DSpark a recorded --draft input and decode plain by default
sourceStates.body:
Snowball RL presets decode without a speculative-decoding draft by default. A run serves the frozen Dr. Doom DSpark draft with `--draft dspark-dr-doom`, and `--draft none` runs plain decoding. Each preset lists the drafts it can serve and may name one as its default. A draft becomes a preset's default through the documented default-change workflow after `--draft` runs pass that preset's control comparison.

`--draft` is a run input beside `--init` and `--sft`. It is part of the run name and `run_inputs.json`, it appears in the Marina run label, and `rl_gate` rebuilds the candidate's configuration with it, so a gated candidate is compared against plain controls and its report lists the draft keys as configuration changes. Control runs reject `--draft`. Each draft records the initial weights it was trained for, and a run serves it only when the run's initial weights have the same artifact identity. A requested draft for other weights is refused, and a default draft is left off. Colocated layouts serve no draft. With `--draft`, `--set` may change only the proposal count; `--set generator.speculative_decoding` without `--draft` still describes an unregistered draft in full.

With the draft as the default, controls would be collected with it, and the comparison would measure plain decoding as the change rather than the draft. The draft has no learning-quality comparison yet. One `speed-medium` run with four proposals passed the speed and policy-mismatch KL guards against four plain controls ([gate report](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-02a%2Fmarin%2Fusers%2Fpower%2Fcheckpoints%2Fsnowball-rl%2Fspeed-medium-da9cc74fcc-in-9bb30c01%2Fgate-n1-e067447cc5-defaults-19d432b0-evidence-21f4a03c%2F2026.11.13%2Fgate_report.md)).

The Snowball revision is 2026.11.25.1. The pinned controls are at 2026.11.06.1, so gated comparisons need controls collected at the new revision. `speed-short` uses the shared 0.75 vLLM memory fraction; add `--set generator.gpu_memory_utilization=0.80` to reproduce the four-proposal screen. Mochi presets have no registered draft and are unchanged.

Follow-up to #11975.

diagnostics.title: [long-loop] Opposite SFT→RL Micro210 deltas: Mochi .123 vs Snowball round 1
diagnostics.body:
## TL;DR

Two long-loop recipes produced opposite SFT→RL changes on the Micro210 panel. Mochi `.123` (SFT step 400407 → RL final step 22) went from **59.74% to 52.91% pooled (−6.82 pp)** and **68.39% to 58.90% on the 19-benchmark mean (−9.49 pp)** under Micro210 policy `2026.11.20-together` (`8f7ef817`). Snowball long-loop round 1 (SFT 746 → RL 16) went from **40.23% to 45.26% pooled (+5.03 pp)** and **47.98% to 52.16% on the 20-benchmark mean (+4.18 pp)** under its earlier MiniMax-judge policy. Both runs are "Exp1" of their respective series: the first Mochi RL run and the first Snowball long-loop round ([#11337](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11337)). The two comparisons differ in base model, SFT recipe and length, RL pool composition, optimizer and learning rate, batch geometry, checkpoint selection, eval policy, judge and serving stack. Each delta is a sealed observation under its own frozen policy; the pair is not a causal RL comparison.

## Description

This issue records both sides of the comparison from primary evidence: the sealed Micro210 evaluations in [#11337](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11337), the Mochi reward curves in [#12119](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/12119), the SFT mix history in [#12199](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/12199), and the two RL recipes (`specs/rl.yaml` at `0c1e81ca93` for round 1; `rounds/mochi-throughput-train-track1.yaml` on `benfeuer/long-loop-prototype` plus the `.123` resolved launch for Mochi).

Micro210 is 200 tasks across 20 benchmarks expanded to 440 attempt slots (AIME24 and OlympiadBench ×10, GPQA/TBLite/TB2 ×3, others ×1). Scores are heterogeneous partial-credit reward means, not pass@1. Missing grades are absent, not zeros ([#10197](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10197)).

### Setup side by side

### The RL mixes are not identical

Both runs draw from the same two release families — `.123`'s curriculum pins `swe-verified-20261112-v4` (`ec645c79…`) and `smartie-mixed-20261110-v1` (`94f21b06…`), the same pins round 1 consumed — but the mixes differ in four ways. First, the agentic share: round 1 admitted 32 agentic + 32 nonagentic groups per update (50%); `.123` consumed 11 + 21 of 32 (34.4%), matching the Exp4 curriculum's 35% agentic target. Second, `.123` adds `nemotron_if` (a curated retained pool of 54,953 rows) at 15% of groups; round 1 has no Nemotron instruction-following source. Third, the sampler: round 1 drew uniformly within each route pool; `.123` used the domain-weighted sampler with pass-variance weighting and adaptive exploration. Fourth, the pools themselves: round 1 consumed the releases' parquets directly; `.123` consumed the Exp4-family stamped pools (`rl-pools/2026.11.22.2`), re-versioned with grader-fixed source versions. The six nonagentic sources keep identical group shares by construction: round 1's uniform-within-pool expectation is each source's row share × 0.5, which is exactly `.123`'s curriculum weight.

## Hypothesis or Goal

Question: did the same kind of SFT→RL recipe improve Snowball and hurt Mochi? Goal: put both sealed results side by side, identify which design differences could produce opposite deltas, and state what would de-confound the comparison.

## Confounds

Ordered by how much they could move the headline deltas.

1. **The RL mixes differ** (table above): agentic share 50% → 34.4%, a new `nemotron_if` source at 15%, uniform vs pass-variance-weighted sampling with adaptive exploration, and different pool materializations. The Exp4-ancestor pools also carry grader-fixed source versions relative to the parquets round 1 consumed.
2. **Different Micro210 policies and harnesses.** Round 1's rows use the MiniMax-M3 judge policy; Mochi's use `8f7ef817` (GLM-5.3-Flash). Cross-model score levels are not comparable, and even round 1's two evals ran on different harness generations (pre- vs post-repair, different serving geometry). Only within-model deltas are meaningful here.
3. **Optimizer and learning rate.** Mochi trained with MuonH at LR 1e-5 (adam_lr 2.31e-6 for its non-Muon parameters) with clipping disabled; round 1 used AdamW at LR 1e-6 with max_grad_norm 0.5 — a 10× learning-rate difference and a different optimizer family. [#12103](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/12103) plans exactly this ablation for both models.
4. **Different base models and SFT recipes.** Mochi: a different base lineage with a 6,916-update full-A/B hero SFT (special-token LR ×5.66, linear LR). Snowball: the 262K base with a 746-update long-loop mix on the 10/05 full-AB stores plus 20% replay. Starting-point capability differs enormously: under the same GLM policy, Mochi SFT pools 59.7% while round 1's SFT 746 was never evaluated under it (its MiniMax-policy score is 40.2%).
5. **Steps, wall-clock and stop reason.** Round 1 completed 17 updates and died at update-18 admission inside a 12 h budget; `.123` completed 22 updates and stopped on its 10 h wall budget with max_steps 32 unused. Different amounts of RL pressure on different schedules.
6. **Checkpoint selection.** Round 1 published an EMA-best checkpoint under a fully-covered 120/120 validation gate. `.123`'s holdout never reached the 180/200 scored eligibility bar (165–176/200 across all evals), so its published checkpoint is the fallback final step 22, not a validated best. Its own curves ([#12119](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/12119)) show training reward rising (0.547 → 0.713 by update 17) while holdout pass@1 fell from baseline (0.679 → 0.665 at update 15) — the selection rule could not rescue this because coverage, not score, failed the gate.
7. **Eval defects and coverage asymmetries.** Mochi's CRUXEval RL cell is a grader artifact worth −70 pp (#11922); excluding it shrinks the regression from −9.49 to −6.13 pp. TruthfulQA is nearly uninformative (#12060) and moved +10 pp for Mochi but −20 pp for round 1. BixBench is ungraded for Mochi (10 `ValueError` attempts without verifier grades; the credential-guard defect is [#12094](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/12094)) but was scored (0.00 → 0.20) under round 1's policy. Mochi's pooled means use different valid populations (413 vs 428); round 1's use 420 vs 439 scored with different harness generations.
8. **Tiny per-benchmark samples.** Ten distinct tasks per benchmark (100 for AIME24/OlympiadBench, 30 for GPQA/TBLite/TB2); one task moves a 10-task cell by 10 pp, and repeated attempts are not independent tasks.
9. **Serving stacks.** Training and eval ran on different hardware and parallelism (GB200 DP16/EP16 TP1 vs H100 TP1/PP2/CP5/EP8; 5 vs 22 rollout engines; different context windows), which changes rollout distributions and eval reproducibility.
10. **Known policy-reward limitations on shared sources.** Typed `PolicyRewardMeasurement` receipts landed with the first Snowball measurements (`ba083af95a`), including the Smartie finish-task weakness and an empty-think-block effect that depresses the measured reward on the Smartie source. Both runs consume that source at the same expected share (5.8% of groups), but through different samplers, so the limitation enters both training signals differently.

## What this does and doesn't show

Does show: two sealed within-model SFT→RL deltas under each run's own frozen policy; the full design differences; that Mochi's regression survives excluding the defective CRUXEval cell (−7.08 pp on the 17-cell panel); and that the matched-mix analogs (Exp3/Exp4) exist but lack SFT-only baselines.

Does not show: that RL causally helps Snowball and hurts Mochi; any cross-model score comparison (different judges and policies); or that step 22 is Mochi's best available checkpoint (it is a fallback selected by coverage failure).

De-confounding, in order of leverage:
1. Run the same RL pool and recipe on both models — `.123` already trains on the Exp4 pool family, so an SFT-only Micro210 eval of the Exp4 (or Exp3) SFT checkpoint under a common policy would give a matched-mix delta on the Snowball side.
2. Re-evaluate both selected checkpoints on the repaired Micro210 policy `2026.11.23-together` now in flight ([#12069](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/12069): CRUXEval frozen graders #11922, TruthfulQA option shuffle #12060, IFBench checker #11926, BixBench judge relay #12094, Pi MCP adapter #12122, provisioning #11787), with a reference rescore to quantify per-cell policy effects.
3. The optimizer/LR ablation planned in [#12103](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/12103).
4. Paired per-prompt comparison of holdout updates on shared scored tasks, as proposed on [#12119](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/12119).

* Mochi `.123`: [resolved launch](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-08a%2Fmarin%2Fusers%2Fbenfeuer%2Fmochi-long-loop%2Flong-loop%2Fmochi-throughput-train-track1%2F2026.11.23.123%2Fresolved-launch.yaml); recipe `rounds/mochi-throughput-train-track1.yaml` on `benfeuer/long-loop-prototype`; [curriculum code](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/benfeuer/long-loop-prototype/experiments/post_training/task_curation/exp4_curriculum.py)
* Seals: [Mochi final 22](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-08a%2Fmarin%2Fusers%2Fbenfeuer%2Fmochi-long-loop-evaluations%2Fseals%2Fmochi123-final22-micro210-2026.11.23.2-20261124%2Fmanifest.json); [round-1 RL16 evaluation](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-08a%2Fmarin%2Fusers%2Fbenfeuer%2Flong-loop%2Flong-loop%2Freport%2F2026.11.12.12%2Fevaluation.json); [Exp4 corrected](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-08a%2Fmarin%2Fusers%2Fbenfeuer%2Flong-loop-exp4%2Fevidence%2Fmicro210-step36-eot-seal100%2Fmanifest.json); [Exp3 step 20](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-08a%2Fmarin%2Fusers%2Fbenfeuer%2Flong-loop-exp3%2Fpermanent-archive%2F2026.11.18%2Fmicro210-step20-seal73%2Fmanifest.json); [Exp5 RL 22](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-02a%2Fmarin%2Fusers%2Fbenfeuer%2Flong-loop-exp5%2Fevidence%2Fmicro210-rl22-seal156%2Fmanifest.json)

Filer links require Marina login; raw `s3://` paths appear inline beside each link.

## Decision Log

* Comparator: Snowball long-loop round 1 (SFT 746 → RL 16), per the 2026-11-24 user ruling, replacing the initially proposed Exp5 pairing. Exp5 remains as context because it is the only Snowball run evaluated under the same GLM policy as Mochi, but it uses a different RL curriculum (`exp5-rl@2026.11.20`).
* Analog: Exp4 is named the closest matched-RL-mix run because `.123`'s curriculum identity is `long-loop/exp4-rl@2026.11.18`; Exp3 is the near match. Neither has an SFT-only Micro210 eval, so no matched-mix SFT→RL delta is reported and none was launched (read-only task).
* `.123`'s batch is 32 groups × 8 samples (256 trajectories/update) per its resolved launch (`train_batch_size: 32`) and logged `consumed/sequences: 256` per update.
* Pool-count provenance: the per-source table uses the round-1 release manifests and `.123`'s curriculum weights; the materialized `rl-pools/2026.11.22.2` manifest is the source of truth for exact counts and was not readable in the drafting session.

## Conclusion

Round 1's +5.03 pp pooled / +4.18 pp benchmark-mean gain and `.123`'s −6.82 pp pooled / −9.49 pp mean drop are real sealed observations, each under its own frozen eval policy. Every layer that could produce the difference also differs: RL mix and sampler, optimizer and learning rate, base model and SFT recipe, run length and stop reason, checkpoint selection, eval policy and harness, and one Mochi eval cell that is a grader defect worth −70 pp. The records support "opposite deltas, heavily confounded" — not "RL helps Snowball and hurts Mochi". The matched-pool SFT-only baselines (Exp3/Exp4) and the repaired Micro210 policy re-evaluation are the cheapest next measurements.

diagnostics.title: [experiment] Reduce Mochi SFT doom loops with online FTPO
diagnostics.body:
## TL;DR

Measure exact repetitive tails in Mochi SFT step 400407, then test whether online FTPO can halve per-domain incidence while retaining native task correctness. Baseline measurement precedes training.

## Description

Adapt the [Dr. Doom campaign](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9691) to Mochi. Preserve the exact tail-loop detector and FTPO objective. Use TP1/BF16 serving and Mochi's MuonH/R3 training path. The fixed, hashed evaluation panel covers math, instruction following, coding, reasoning_gym, structured outputs, and STEM MCQ. All graders are programmatic and fail closed.

## Hypothesis or Goal

For each target domain, obtain a post-training loop upper bound no greater than half its confirmed baseline count on identical prompts. Extend low-incidence 32K cohorts from 128 to 256; fewer than 10 confirmed loops after extension makes a domain non-target. Non-target upper bounds may increase by at most three. Per-domain correctness may lose at most max(3, 5% of N) passes; pooled correctness may lose at most 2% of the panel.

## Status

Native-rendered cohort v2 is published and verified (manifest SHA-256 `1c2f2b83a3b895b518e7745d3a1fe05af857f56273449c6a3aad9087f9354af3`). Corrected S0 was submitted November 24 at 19:45:04 EST, runtime `2026.11.24.4`, source `1661a15e9f`, for 128 GB200 on cw-us-east-08a at production priority. Coordinator and GPU child are running. No valid incidence count is available yet; training remains pending.

The first S0 attempt was cancelled at 19:25 EST because preparation omitted the native answer-format instruction when hashing prompts. Its outputs and v1 hash table are excluded. V2 exactly matches the saved native prompt; all 512 original math tasks remain eligible.

Seal the full baseline and sparse-domain reserves before S1. The executor clock remains November 24 17:46 EST through November 26 17:46 EST; start no training after November 26 13:46 EST.

## Links

- Prior campaign: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9691
- Source branch: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/benfeuer/mochi-doom-ftpo
- Logbook: https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/codex/77-mochi-doom-ftpo/logbooks/77-mochi-doom-ftpo/notebook.md

## Decision Log

- Freeze baseline prompts and detector before choosing target domains.
- Keep circular but nonperiodic reasoning out of the exact-loop objective; report length stops and open reasoning spans separately.

## Conclusion

Pending measurement.

diagnostics.title: [post-training] Add loop guards for agent traces: SFT repetition filters, stall stops, wait demonstrations, loop metrics

labels.name: evals
labels.description: Evaluations: benchmarks, leaderboard, eval gates / metrics

diagnostics.body:
## TL;DR

Add loop guards for agent traces at four layers: SFT data filters, wait demonstrations, an episode stop on stalls, and a loop metric in evals. Then test the RL and decoding guards Marin already has. The design follows IFM's [`repetition_check.py`](https://github.com/ifm-ai/process_entry/blob/main/repetition_check.py) and the K2-Horizon results ([arXiv 2611.21003](https://arxiv.org/html/2611.21003v1)). The full survey of Marin's current loop guards, with citations, is [here](https://gistpreview.github.io/?3d44de572b8babfc08f96ac90a05b109).

## Background

- **SFT filter (main).** The only agent-loop filter is `has_stalled_tool_call` in `lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/chat_normalize.py`, added in #9259. It drops a record on the third identical tool call after two identical replies, within one user turn, and fired on 101 of 210,031 sampled conversations.
  - It misses Terminus-2 traces, because terminal output is stored as user turns and each one resets the counter.
  - It misses spread-out repetition.
- **Ending episodes (missing).** Nothing ends an episode when the agent repeats itself. The rolloutengine stops only at turn, token or time limits. Terminus-2's `turn_callback` can return EARLY_TERMINATION, but no callback uses it.
- **RL penalties (unused).** Vendored SkyRL has two loop penalties, both off by default. The loop-credit penalty was swept in #9599 and no strength stood out. No recipe enables the antithrash penalty for repeated actions.
- **Doom loops (in flight).** #9691 and #12240 target repeated token suffixes at the end of a response. They don't cover repeated actions, and `loop_audit.py` lives only on branch `benfeuer/mochi-doom-ftpo`.
- **Evals (no metric).** There is no standing loop metric. #7743 measured median exact-duplicate tool-call fractions of 20–37%, but only once.
- **IFM's evidence.**
  - RL cut exact repeats inside Terminal-Bench interrupt loops from 61.8% to 0.3%. Trials with a loop barely changed, from 12.9% to 11.6%.
  - SFT demonstrations of waiting after unchanged output brought interrupt loops below 1%. In IFM's midtraining data, the agent waited 0 times out of 446 such moments.

## Proposed work

1. **IFM-style rules in `chat_normalize.py`.**
   - Reject 8 consecutive identical name+args tool calls, whatever the replies.
   - Reject a call that occurs at least 10 times, accounts for at least 30% of assistant turns, and appears in a run of at least 3 identical calls.
   - For Terminus-2 records, reject at least 8 consecutive identical normalized assistant messages when one preceding observation accounts for at least 80% of the run.
   - Keep #9259's exemption for retries that get a different reply.
   - Report fire rates per source, and hand-check a sample for precision.
2. **Wait demonstrations.**
   - Audit the SFT and midtraining mixes for what the agent does after unchanged terminal output.
   - Add Terminus-2 rows that wait or poll on long-running commands, next to the recovery rows from #10888.
   - Generate them in a real-clock environment, because ShellSim sleeps take no wall time (#10159).
3. **Stall stop in the rolloutengine.**
   - Add a stop reason such as `REPEAT_STALL` that fires after 3 consecutive identical action batches with identical observations.
   - Grade the task anyway, so work done before the stall still earns credit.
   - Add it to the #12190 port list, and either confirm or remove the "thrashing detector" that the #6341 checklist marks done.
4. **Loop metrics in evals.**
   - Merge `loop_audit.py` to main.
   - Add to the #10197 eval policy: loop count and upper bound, the exact-duplicate tool-call fraction (the #7743 method), and an interrupt-loop count on Terminal-Bench.
   - Report repeats inside loops and the share of trials with a loop separately.
5. **Antithrash ablation.**
   - Enable `antithrash` on one agentic RL recipe.
   - Add an option to apply it only to otherwise-correct trajectories.
   - Track both measures from item 4.
6. **Decoding checks.**
   - Run a paired comparison of `repetition_penalty` 1.0 against 1.1 on the snowball-sft eval and the curriculum-RL policy.
   - Land #12254 with a full set of stop tokens.

## Done when

- [ ] `chat_normalize.py` has the three IFM-style rules with tests, and per-source fire rates are posted here.
- [ ] A wait-behaviour audit of the SFT and midtraining mixes is posted, and a wait-demonstration source is in the SFT mix.
- [ ] The rolloutengine records a repeat-stall stop reason, and the #6341 "thrashing detector" entry is confirmed or corrected.
- [ ] Eval reports show loop counts, the duplicate tool-call fraction, and the Terminal-Bench interrupt-loop share.
- [ ] Antithrash ablation results are posted with both loop measures.
- [ ] Results of the paired `repetition_penalty` test are posted, and #12254 has merged.

Related: #9259, #9599, #9691, #12240, #7743, #10197, #12190, #6341, #10888, #10159, #12254.

diagnostics.title: [rl] Reduce Snowball train-long memory and isolate run state
diagnostics.body:
Snowball `train-long` packs samples and uses two context-parallel ranks with KV all-gather for both policy and reference. A 25-update Reno proof completed all updates on 40 H100s with this memory configuration. The CP1 run exhausted memory in update 24. [Memory proof](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin-snowball-rl/runs/ad32076d128a)

Published task selections are read-only inputs. The runner checks that they exist and rejects steps that write to the same path. Launcher NCCL rendezvous is scoped to the Iris job and attempt. The gate estimates GPU-hours using the configured GPU count and the time from the first recorded workload start to native job completion.

diagnostics.title: [evals][eval_policy] Eval Policy Changes for Nov 30 Update
diagnostics.body:
We are targeting an update to our post-training eval policy on November 30th, 2026\. The new policy will focus on improving coverage over key capabilities, especially factuality and math/science reasoning. The purpose of this issue is to invite the community to provide feedback on the listed evals and suggest changes to our implementations.

## Changes to In-Distribution Benchmarks

The tables below list the major changes to our the in-distribution benchmark composition.

* Benchmarks slated for **removal** will be taken out of the policy with high probability,
* Benchmarks flagged for **changes** need some repair to make them work on more recent versions of main,  
* Benchmarks marked as **potential additions** have draft implementations and may be included in the next round.

We will select our in-distribution benchmarks to collectively cover the capabilities necessary for Mochi to do well on our out-of-distribution benchmarks (listed below). Beginning in 2027, we hope to make this process more data-driven, but for the Nov 30 policy, we will select ID benchmarks based on:

1. Our assessment of each benchmark’s quality and appropriateness for hillclimbing,  
2. Whether an eval can be run reliably in our eval infrastructure,  
3. The resource cost of running the eval,  
4. The wall clock time of running the eval,  
5. Coverage over our out-of-distribution benchmarks,  
6. Whether we find eval contamination in our training data.

In the policy announcement on Nov 30, we will explain why particular evaluations were included or excluded. Our full set of in-distribution evals must run in no more than 24 hours for Mochi, and our eval lite subset used for model development must run in no more than 3 hours.

The proposed changes favor more recent evaluations (which have a smaller chance of contamination and reflect modern capability priorities) while increasing implicit weight on scientific tasks. This includes the addition of a number of benchmarks specifically targeting scientific knowledge and reasoning. New core capability benchmarks target factuality (SimpleQA Verified, FACTS Parametric/Grounding), instruction following (MultiChallenge) and realistic long context tasks (LongBench v2). We have not significantly changed the set of agentic evaluations in this round and will instead focus on reliable, performant implementations of our existing evals, with a few exceptions.

### Removals

| Benchmark | Domain | Proposed Change | Brief Justification |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| [MATH-500](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/50d4f6f/experiments/evaluation/benchmarks/math.py#L188) | Math | Remove | Close to saturation on Snowball and Mochi comparisons. |
| [GSM8K](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/50d4f6f/experiments/evaluation/benchmarks/gsm8k.py#L32) | Math | Remove | Close to saturation on Snowball and Mochi comparisons. |
| [HumanEval+](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/50d4f6f/experiments/evaluation/benchmarks/code.py#L107) | Non-Agentic Code | Might remove | Close to saturation on Snowball and Mochi comparisons. |
| [MBPP+](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/50d4f6f/experiments/evaluation/benchmarks/code.py#L119) | Non-Agentic Code | Remove | Close to saturation on Snowball and Mochi comparisons. |
| [PIQA](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/50d4f6f/experiments/evaluation/benchmarks/multiple_choice.py#L152) | Reasoning | Remove | Close to saturation on Snowball and Mochi comparisons. |
| [BoolQ](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/50d4f6f/experiments/evaluation/benchmarks/multiple_choice.py#L135) | Reading Comprehension | Remove | Close to saturation on Snowball and Mochi comparisons. |

## Changes to Out-of-Distribution Benchmarks

Our previous eval policy listed AAII v4.3, Terminal Bench Science v0.1 and DeepSWE v1.1 as out-of-distribution benchmarks. We largely retain this set of evals, with some changes, notably the inclusion of LAB-Bench v2.

Below, we list the full set of evals we consider out of distribution. As a reminder, we do not run these evaluations until the completion of a Marin post-training round and do not look at any individual tasks. The single exception to this rule is the evals team that implements the public subsets of these evaluations for us to report. The evals team does not share any data from the implementation testing with the training team and will protect any data from testing runs from Marin’s training engineers and their agents.

🤖
# Research

The round-one entry records pinned SFT/RL sources and configs, an immutable checkpoint revision, Micro eval policy and scores (439/440 attempts scored), and archive receipts. [PR #11120](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11120) contains the open long-loop implementation and reports the RL admission failure. Issue #11337 has no later measured recipe or specific code defect to address.

**Relevant code**
- [`run_spec.py#L71-L113`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12fefdef4a1e10a17b1ee33d54de49efb2e2271f/experiments/post_training/long_loop/run_spec.py#L71-L113) — resolves and validates pinned configs.
- [`audit_results.py#L15-L92`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12fefdef4a1e10a17b1ee33d54de49efb2e2271f/experiments/post_training/long_loop/eval_runtime/audit_results.py#L15-L92) — audits scored and unscored attempts.
- [`archive.py#L72-L98`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12fefdef4a1e10a17b1ee33d54de49efb2e2271f/experiments/post_training/long_loop/archive.py#L72-L98) — seals and verifies evidence.

# Proposed Fix

Keep this issue open as the measured-recipe index. For each new run: (1) pin the SFT/RL source commits, complete run specs, exact data files and mixture weights, then validate the pins; (2) publish the selected immutable checkpoint revision, Micro eval policy, scored/unscored counts, both aggregate means, benchmark scores, and provenance/archive receipts with explicit gaps; (3) add the recipe as a comment and update the summary table. Assign a new recipe version whenever code, data, sampling, or grading changes.

🤖 The recipe ledger is [#11337](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11337). Its first entry records the completed round-1 model, pinned SFT/RL configs and data mixes, the Micro policy and all 20 benchmark scores, the public HF revision, and the private provenance archive.

Under the user's subsequent explicit cleanup request, removed 12 superseded native checkpoints: SFT steps 1, 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600 and 700; abandoned run `2026.11.11.2` RL steps 1–2; and run `2026.11.12.5` RL steps 12 and 14. This removed 173,721 current objects totaling 6,439,134,545,120 bytes (6.44 TB; physical billing reduction was not measured). All 12 prefixes verify empty. Retained SFT step 746 (`2026.11.09.12`) and selected RL step 16 (`2026.11.12.5`) match their pre-cleanup object sets, sizes and ETags. Base weights, HF exports, data, logs and the evidence archive remain. Fifty-two metadata backups were read back and hash-verified before deleting the checkpoints. Receipt: `s3://marin-us-east-08a/marin/users/benfeuer/long-loop/evidence/20261113-intermediate-checkpoint-cleanup/completed.json` ([Filer](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-08a%2Fmarin%2Fusers%2Fbenfeuer%2Flong-loop%2Fevidence%2F20261113-intermediate-checkpoint-cleanup%2Fcompleted.json)).

This is a manual cleanup record. The original archive's incomplete-evidence flags remain unchanged; it does not certify W&B provider completeness or erase the unscored DNA assembly attempt UID399.

🤖

### Long-loop round 2, November 2026

SFT completed 204 optimizer updates, numbered 0–203, and retained native checkpoint 203. RL completed 20 updates and selected checkpoint 20 by eligible validation-reward EMA. Export, final evaluation, public HF upload and the private evidence archive completed with limitations. The original coordinator failed at its report coverage gate after successful RL, export and evaluation; CPU post-processing completed without replaying training or policy sampling. The completion receipt is dated November 15, 2026, 10:49:53.982839 UTC (05:49:53.982839 EST).

Model: [open-athena/Snowball-LongLoop-Round2-2026.11.14.13 at `6546ba2d5a1d44992d6376d4c51c1a69f16b1d10`](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-LongLoop-Round2-2026.11.14.13/tree/6546ba2d5a1d44992d6376d4c51c1a69f16b1d10), OpenMDW-1.1. The completion receipt records 49 verified files / 39 weight shards matching the producer export.

#### Configs and launch

No round-2 downloadable recipe tarball or dedicated recipe-bundle manifest was found in the long-loop evidence prefix or round-2 archive inventory. The round-1 tarball describes a different recipe. Round 2 retains frozen input directories and consumed configs; this entry does not certify a self-contained, run-ready bundle.

SFT input directory: `s3://marin-us-east-08a/marin/users/benfeuer/long-loop/evidence/20261113-exp2-full11-inputs/20261113-exp2-full11/` ([Filer](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-08a%2Fmarin%2Fusers%2Fbenfeuer%2Flong-loop%2Fevidence%2F20261113-exp2-full11-inputs%2F20261113-exp2-full11%2F)); `round1.yaml` SHA-256 `1a71eb7a4f138972cae61e0db357f66cecec7e6887156e267f548f1b83631e97`. RL/eval input directory: `s3://marin-us-east-08a/marin/users/benfeuer/long-loop/evidence/20261114-exp2-recovery13/inputs/` ([Filer](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-08a%2Fmarin%2Fusers%2Fbenfeuer%2Flong-loop%2Fevidence%2F20261114-exp2-recovery13%2Finputs%2F)); `round1.yaml` SHA-256 `5f811e728dff9d3ef2737f1d7ca5ee3fffaa0abdf259cb79aca56ae1fdc912a2`. The historical filenames remain `round1.yaml`; their declared recipe name is `long-loop/round2`. Each top-level YAML pins its stage files by SHA-256. The archive manifest below pins copied consumed configs, resolved spec, attempt evidence and data accounting; it is an evidence manifest, not a recipe-bundle manifest.

| Stage | Exact source and config | Measured recipe |
|---|---|---|
| Initial model | [Snowball base `058ecaf27b9e4f37219df221a51e7d490d58ec3d`](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/snowball-67b-a2b-base-262k-qk175-skew8/tree/058ecaf27b9e4f37219df221a51e7d490d58ec3d) | Frozen weights-only initializer; tokenizer `marin-community/marin-tokenizer-tools@3f6879acdaf3dae7874b2d48c7d11b9d8c6faf09` |

Consumed Adam LR 5e-5, cosine schedule, betas 0.9/0.95; serialized-chat assistant loss; sequential packing capped at 256 documents; continuous causal replay |
| RL | [base source `038ad7f188a889dfed07cac9a29fe34eabd7e5cd`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/038ad7f188a889dfed07cac9a29fe34eabd7e5cd); frozen RL directory above, `rl.yaml` and archived `objects/rl/resolved-launch.yaml` | 80 learner + 176 rollout H100; learner TP1/PP2/CP5/EP8, a2a; AdamW LR 1e-6; 102,400 context; 16,384 output tokens/turn; 128 turns; temperature 0.7, top-p 1.0; TITO/TIS/router replay |

Both measured builds recorded `dirty: true`: SFT tree `00a8f56ce2`, RL/eval tree `266e04d2a1`. Source commits identify their bases, not clean-build equivalence. The production seal tag [`experiments/exp2-rl20-2026.11.15`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/experiments/exp2-rl20-2026.11.15) resolves to post-processing commit [`4913edc4884291fc54d7023eda66edc38b9a9e2e`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/4913edc4884291fc54d7023eda66edc38b9a9e2e); it did not produce the sampled policies.

The agent harness is [Pi and its MCP adapter](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/038ad7f188a889dfed07cac9a29fe34eabd7e5cd/vendor/harbor/src/harbor/agents/installed/pi.py), Pi 0.87.0/MCP 7.0.0. TITO preserves sampled token IDs, TIS applies truncated importance sampling, and router replay reuses sampled expert routes. SWE uses UID 10001, harness-owned checkout/setup, protected `/testbed` and a trusted grading interpreter; the consumed config explicitly routes `long-loop-smartie-swesmith` to `harbor_trial`.

RL consumes exactly 32 SWE + 32 non-agentic groups per update, eight samples per group (512 trajectories), with maximum staleness of two optimizer updates. Its explicit budget is 10 h from the first completed optimizer step, with a 1,800-second drain margin. Validation and native saves occur every two updates. Selection uses an EMA with span five (alpha 1/3) and requires all 120 validation tasks scored; selected step 20 scored 120/120. Retention is last three plus protected best. Final evaluation and HF publication use the same selected checkpoint.

The recorded launches used the following spec paths and versions in separate source worktrees. These are historical commands, not a newly validated standalone replay recipe:

```bash
# SFT base 442bf9d878…; frozen full11 directory at the path below.
export MARIN_PREFIX=s3://marin-us-east-08a/marin/users/benfeuer/long-loop
export MARIN_TEMP_PREFIX=s3://marin-us-east-08a/tmp
uv run python -m experiments.post_training.long_loop \
  --spec experiments/post_training/long_loop/runtime-inputs/20261113-exp2-full11/round1.yaml \
  --through archive --version 2026.11.13.11 \
  --validation-output experiments/post_training/long_loop/runtime-inputs/20261113-exp2-full11/validation \
  --max-concurrent 1 --run

# RL/eval base 038ad7f188…; adopts historical SFT203 and its corrected HF handoff.
uv run python -m experiments.post_training.long_loop \
  --spec experiments/post_training/long_loop/runtime-inputs/20261114-exp2-recovery13/round1.yaml \
  --through archive --version 2026.11.14.13 \
  --validation-output experiments/post_training/long_loop/runtime-inputs/20261114-exp2-recovery13/validation \
  --max-concurrent 1 --run
```

No launch was submitted while preparing this entry. Reproduction requires fresh output versions, the frozen inputs, Marin storage access and configured secret bindings (`HF_TOKEN`, `WANDB_API_KEY`, `CW_KEY_ID`/`CW_KEY_SECRET`, `DAYTONA_RL_API_KEY`, `DAYTONA_EVAL_API_KEY`, `DAYTONA_TARGET=us`, `TOGETHER_API_KEY`). It also requires resolving both dirty build identities and adopting the corrected SFT HF handoff pinned by `adopted-handoff.json` in the RL input directory; commit bases alone do not certify equivalent builds. Credential values are omitted. The RL/eval coordinator's report-coverage failure is preserved; completion is established by the replacement receipt below.

#### Exact data mixes

SFT retains 377 source components and all 19 weight-schedule entries in the frozen input directories: `sft-components.json` SHA-256 `d372def486ced1418d1ad63bd9f50959f463430ecbcd83029d6db12dfe0ad493` and `sft-train_weights.json` SHA-256 `e954bba2b54492ab3af6ff56a735e4dcaea53a6599f61c5480baae9a57d9bdcd`. The 70,562,321-byte `realized-samples.jsonl` has SHA-256 `58713a89dd097645ef82a5b8307cb52c9a08cde7836d44824e9ebfa06deed20d`. | Benchmark | Constant reply | Score (%) | Round 1 | Round 2 | Round 3 | Base | Snowball v0.1 |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| TruthfulQA | `\boxed{A}` | 100 | 70 | 80 | 70 | 20 | 90 |
| GPQA Diamond | `B` | 50 | 56.7 | 56.7 | 43.3 | 33.3 | 66.7 |

The other ten answer benchmarks score 0 for every reply. The six agentic benchmarks were not run.

- TruthfulQA: the generated-choice prompts list the options in `mc2_targets` order, which starts with a true answer. Option A is true in every task: 10 in Micro210, 41 in Mini840, 817 rows of `truthfulqa/truthful_qa`. A seeded shuffle of each task's options would remove this. The full policy's MC2 likelihood scoring does not depend on order.
- MMLU-Pro: without `answer is (X)` or `Answer: X`, the extractor takes the last standalone capital A-J, so `I don't know.` counts as option I, the key of 4 tasks.
- GPQA Diamond: 5 of the 10 drawn keys are B.
- IFBench: the prepared rows grade it with the `evalchemy` wheel of `runtime-v4`, whose IFBench checkers are byte-identical to `vendor/evalchemy` before #10423. In one of the 10 tasks (key 278, the capitals of European countries north of 45°) a correct reply cannot pass: the checker's list leaves out Kyiv, so the 28 correct capitals score 0 and the 27 without Kyiv score 1.

This does not show that a round guesses. On these 10 tasks, the three benchmarks cannot tell a round from a constant below the floor. They carry 8.7 of Round 3's 41.07 points. Without them, Rounds 1-3, the base and Snowball v0.1 average 49.8, 44.7, 38.1, 13.3 and 40.3%.

from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download

path = hf_hub_download("open-athena/Marin-Micro-Eval-210", "data/validation.parquet", repo_type="dataset",

        labels.append(config["spec"]["doc"]["mc2_targets"]["labels"][0])
print(f"option A is true in {sum(labels)} of {len(labels)} TruthfulQA tasks")

The uncertainty calculation follows the prior Exp3 seal and [#10197](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10197). Each benchmark uses the conservative task-level SEM bound `s = 0.5/sqrt(10*0.9)`, including the 90% valid-trial allowance. With scored fractions `r_b`, means `m_b` and weights `w_b=1/20`, set `mu=sum(w_b*r_b*m_b)`, `delta=sum(w_b*(1-r_b))` and `sigma=sqrt(sum((w_b*r_b*s)^2))`. The Imbens–Manski critical value solves `Phi(c+delta/sigma)-Phi(-c)=0.95`; here `c=1.9381`. The interval is `[mu-c*sigma, mu+c*sigma+delta]`, clipped to [0,1]; benchmark intervals use one cell. Identified bounds assign missing rewards values in [0,1] without sampling uncertainty, so they are not confidence intervals. Repetitions are not independent tasks; these intervals do not measure serving-stack reproducibility.

12193.body:
🤖 Holistic review of 8f42cbc4ff1885b9afd5bfea8ef0532518539048.

This PR adds two opt-in Megatron policy options. `output_projection_chunk_size` computes PPO token log-probs and entropy through a token-chunked output projection, so the full token-by-vocabulary tensor never exists. `memory_profile` runs a warm-Adam capacity check before rollout admission. The chunked projection is sound. The capacity check cannot run under the default colocated placement, and it measures a sequence length chosen by hand instead of the trainer's resolved maximum. Fix those two gaps before merging. Then the check matches what the body promises: failing before rollouts instead of after.

**Before.** Megatron's `GPTModel` returned full `[B, T, V]` logits. `MegatronModelWrapper` then computed log-probs and entropy with the `logprob_chunk_size` kernels. Those kernels bound softmax temporaries, but the projection and its backward still materialize the full vocabulary. Nothing checked trainer memory before the first real update.

**Design.** The wrapper now passes MCore 0.18's `output_processor` hook (confirmed in the pinned `megatron_core-0.18.0` wheel, `gpt_model.py:690`). `_output_statistics` returns `[B, T, 2]` statistics in place of logits. `_ProjectedSoftmax` recomputes each chunk in backward. With `gradient_accumulation_fusion` it hands TE's dummy wgrad back once, so the fp32 `main_grad` accumulates natively. Target construction moved into `packed_next_token_targets` and is shared with the existing packed path. `_unpack_statistics` reproduces the existing drop-last-position contract. Under CP, `unpack_packed_token_values` keeps gradient only for the local slice. That matches `AllGatherCPTensor.backward`, so gradient scale is unchanged. On startup, `RayPPOTrainer._train_loop` now calls `profile_train_memory` on every policy rank before `_init_weight_sync`. That method snapshots model, master shards, optimizer, scaler, scheduler, and RNG to host memory, runs one cold step and then warm steps at each token count, writes per-rank JSON under `export_path/trainer-sizing/`, and restores everything.

**Evidence and limits.** I ran the new CPU tests locally with the `skyrl-wheel` CI command: `test_projected_softmax.py` and `test_trainer_memory_profile.py` pass (18 tests). These tests cover value/gradient parity, the no-full-vocabulary allocation bound, fused `main_grad` accumulation, and state restoration. Run alone, `test_megatron_config.py` fails with "Policy loss registry is not populated", and its existing FA2 test fails the same way, so the failure looks environmental. CI `skyrl-wheel` was still pending. No GPU or Megatron run exercises `_output_statistics` or `profile_train_memory`. Nothing in the repository enables either option yet. #12194 is stacked on this PR and only widens the optimizer allowlist.

**Findings**

- **1. Blocker:** `vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/trainer.py:1222` runs the profile before `self.policy_model.backload_to_gpu()`. With `trainer.placement.colocate_all` (the default in `ppo_base_config.yaml` and in the `Placement` recipe section), `_init_models` has already called `policy_model.offload_to_cpu`, and `offload_megatron_model_to_cpu` resizes every DDP `param_data` storage to 0. `profile_train_memory` then snapshots empty parameters and runs forward on an offloaded model. Any colocated run that enables sizing fails at startup or measures a model that is not resident. The test accepts exactly this configuration: `test_chunked_sizing_accepts_ppo_and_rejects_incompatible_execution` validates `memory_profile.enabled` on the default `colocate_all=true` config. Reject `colocate_all` together with `memory_profile.enabled` in `validate_megatron_config` and flip that test. Alternatively, run the profile after the colocated backload (inference asleep) and offload again afterwards.
- **2. Should fix:** `vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/workers/megatron/megatron_worker.py:620` sizes the largest step at `memory_profile.max_sequence_length`, a second hand-set length. The body says sizing covers "each configured token count plus `trainer.algorithm.max_seq_len`", and the first commit's YAML comment said the same, but no code reads `trainer.algorithm.max_seq_len`. `driver_validation.py:269` resolves that value from `generation_context_limit(cfg.generator)` before `validate_megatron_config` runs at `:322`. A recipe that sets `max_sequence_length` below the generator's context limit passes sizing and can still OOM on the first long trajectory after rollouts, which is the failure this check exists to prevent. Drop `TrainerMemoryProfile.max_sequence_length` (and its sidecar/validation entries) and use `cfg.trainer.algorithm.max_seq_len` as the maximum. The `max_position_embeddings` check and the `valid_token_counts` bound can then compare against that one value.
- **3. Should fix:** `vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/config/validation.py:49` rejects only the `ftpo`/`dpo` loss types for chunking. Top-K distillation (`trainer.algorithm.distillation`) passes validation, and chunking then fails in `loss_func` (`megatron_model_wrapper.py:624`) on the first training step, after rollouts have run. Sizing has the same gap: the synthetic microbatch carries no `distillation` evidence, so a distillation run can pass sizing while it under-measures. The compatibility rules are now split across `validate_megatron_config`, `_output_statistics`, `collection_func`, and `loss_func`. Put them in `validate_megatron_config` with the `algorithm.get("distillation") is not None` idiom from `driver_validation.py:179`, covering both options. Then drop the per-microbatch `ValueError` re-checks or reduce them to asserts.

<!-- marin-holistic-review:8f42cbc4ff1885b9afd5bfea8ef0532518539048 -->

🤖 PR description: it says the capacity check measures "at each configured token count plus `trainer.algorithm.max_seq_len`". The code measures the configured counts plus `trainer.policy.megatron_config.memory_profile.max_sequence_length`, which validation requires to be set explicitly (`profile_train_memory` in `megatron_worker.py`). Please name the field the code actually reads.

<!-- marin-correctness-review -->

🤖 Removed unrelated sizing guard assertions, an exact error-message match, and a stale test docstring while retaining the trained generation-bound regression. Corrected the packed scoring comment. Focused SkyRL tests: 20 passed. Pre-commit's Pyrefly step reported missing dependencies in the root `.venv`.

<!-- marin-deslop:8f42cbc4ff1885b9afd5bfea8ef0532518539048 -->

🤖 Closing as fully merged: #12194's squash landed this branch's entire diff on main — the opt-in author schema, the token-chunked output projection, warm-Adam sizing, the colocated backload before profiling, and the trained-generation-bound check. The only delta left on this branch is a deslop commit that pared the sizing test down against the pre-fix test layout, which would remove acceptance and TP1 coverage that main's test_megatron_config.py already carries.

🤖 Note on the record: two commits landed on this branch after the close, pushed while answering the four unresolved review threads above, and they are not on main:

- `857781a951` rejects an active top-K distillation plan at config time when `output_projection_chunk_size` or `memory_profile.enabled` is set, with a behavior test (thread on validation.py resolved above).
- `aee7ab3293` orders the sizing maximum's explicit-positive guard before the trained-bound comparison, which previously made the guard unreachable for null or non-positive values, with a test pin.

If the config-time top-K rejection is still wanted, these two commits need a follow-up route to main; the rest of this PR's diff is indeed fully merged via #12194.

Plan:
1. Pin a repaired Micro210 policy and its prepared table before comparing models. Record immutable hashes, task IDs, judge, serving configuration, scoring rules, and treatment of missing grades. Confirm the CRUXEval, TruthfulQA, and BixBench repairs are present; a draft component alone does not qualify.
2. Evaluate Mochi SFT 400407 and RL 22, plus Snowball round-1 SFT 746 and RL 16, on the same frozen 440 attempt slots under that policy. Publish sealed per-benchmark and pooled results, coverage, paired deltas on jointly scored task IDs, and task-level uncertainty. Keep the earlier policy scores labeled separately.
3. Locate the retained Snowball Exp4 SFT 360 checkpoint and evaluate it with Exp4 RL 36 under the same policy. Exp4 is the closest curriculum analog to Mochi `.123`; publish its SFT→RL delta and the remaining optimizer, sampler, and model differences. Record checkpoint unavailability if the SFT export cannot be recovered.
4. Use those results to narrow the [#12103](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/12103) ablation and the paired Mochi holdout analysis proposed in [#12119](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/12119). Do not infer a model-specific RL effect from the current cross-policy comparison.

Done when the issue links the policy pin and sealed evaluations, reports paired deltas with coverage for both original runs and Exp4 or states its checkpoint blocker, and identifies the remaining controlled experiment.
